title: DSWD urges content creators to be respectful of PWDs
summary: The Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) told content creators to be more respectful of people with mental health conditions.

blocks.text: Every individual with a disability, including those on the autism spectrum or with neurodevelopmental conditions, deserves dignity, respect, privacy, and the utmost care, DSWD said. (Photo from DSWD FB post)
The Department of Social Welfare and Development (DSWD) told content creators to be more respectful of people with mental health conditions.
The agency issued the statement in response to a viral incident wherein the hosts of the podcast Machong Chismisan made fun of people on the autism spectrum.

"Every individual with a disability, including those on the autism spectrum or with neurodevelopmental conditions, deserves dignity, respect, privacy, and the utmost care. Exploiting a person's disability for amusement, ridicule, or online engagement is unacceptable, as it reinforces harmful stereotypes and drives discrimination against a vulnerable group," DSWD spokesperson Assistant Secretary Irene Dumlao said.

"We urge all content creators to exercise responsibility in discussing topics that make fun and violate the rights of vulnerable sectors such as persons with disabilities, whether it is apparent or non-apparent. We need to protect their dignity not only as an act of compassion but also as part of upholding their human rights," she added.
Dumlao said that content creators have the responsibility of fostering inclusive digital spaces and ensuring that they are mindful of the rights of vulnerable people.
The DSWD said that under the Magna Carta for Persons with Disabilities, any act that shames, ridicules, or vilifies a person with disabilities is punishable under the law.
While the agency did not name names, the controversial episode of Machong Chismisan poked fun at Josh Aquino, the son of media personality Kris Aquino.
The hosts of the show have since apologized and taken down the episode following the backlash. —Jean Mangaluz/LDF, GMA News
